TESTIMONY BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON AGRICULTURE, CONSERVATION, AND FORESTRY
IN SUPPORT OF LD 24
Resolve Authorizing the Director of the Bureau of Parks and Lands to Convey Public Lands Parcels in Lincoln Plantation and Sandy River Plantation
February 28, 2025

Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Agriculture, Conservation, and Forestry, my name is Bill Patterson, and I am the Deputy
Director of the Bureau of Parks and Lands (BPL) within the Department of Agriculture,
Conservation and Forestry (DACF). I am speaking in support of LD 24, A Resolve Authorizing
the Director of the Bureau of Parks and Lands to Convey Public Lands Parcels in Lincoln Plantation and Sandy River Plantation.
The resolve would authorize the Bureau of Parks and Lands to convey the State's interest in lease lots in two different locations. In Lincoln Plantation, forty-seven lease lots would be offered for
sale to the current lessees at appraised value. These lots are an administrative burden to BPL and
have no value to the public in their existing uses. The sale of the lots would generate revenue to purchase other Public Lands in Oxford County for public access and conservation values. Out of
respect to the leaseholders whose finances may not enable them to make a purchase, sales would
be voluntary and remain as standing offers until all lots are eventually sold over time.
Because leased camps do not typically receive significant investments or upgrades, the sale of the lease lots is expected to improve many of the existing camps and thus increase Lincoln Plantation's taxable valuation and tax revenue. The sale of these lots would represent a Win for the camp owners, a win for Lincoln Plantation, and a win for the State of Maine.
Since the Bureau drafted LD 24, research has identified an additional fourteen undeveloped lots
wedged in between the 47 lots (See map Fig. 3) that are not currently leased and are too small to be sold as lots for new development. The Bureau requests the Committee consider an
amendment that would include the additional fourteen vacant lots in the authority to sell, but
only as additions to adjacent lots. An amendment could also clarify that the boundaries of all lots
would be determined by survey and should extend to the lake so as not to leave a sliver of Public Lands in front of the sold camp lots.

Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture Conservation and Forestry on LD 24, "Resolve,
Authorizing the Director of the Bureau of Parks and Lands to Convey Public Land Parcels in Lincoln Plantation and Sandy River Plantation"
Public Hearing: January 28, 2025
Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, esteemed members of the Committee. My name is
Senator Russell Black and I am here to introduce L.D. 24 "Resolve, Authorizing the Director of
the Bureau of Parks and Lands to Convey Public Land Parcels in Lincoln Plantation and Sandy
River Plantation."
This resolve authorizes the Director of the Bureau of Parks and Lands, within the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry, to implement land transactions at two key locations. First, it allows the Director to convey 61 leased lots in Lincoln Plantation. This number has increased from the original amount of 47 as the department identified l4 additional lots in between the initial 47 proposed for sale. The proceeds from these sales will go toward purchasing additional conservation land in Oxford County.
The second part of the bill authorizes a value-for-value land exchange in Sandy River Plantation. This exchange would provide a deeded right-of-way across an adjacent parcel of land.
This bill balances responsible land management with long-term conservation priorities. You will
hear more specific details from the department on what this resolve aims to do.
Thank you for your attention to this legislation.
